turns.doctor_question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Well, I guess I'm here because the clinic doctor got on me about my eating. I mean, most days I just keep it simple. I usually just have coffee in the morning, maybe a few bites of something between painting jobs, and... a small dinner, if I'm not too busy with my class paperwork. It's just my normal routine, but they wanted me to come talk to you.

turns.doctor_question: Are you afraid of gaining weight?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I suppose I am. It's just... if I eat something heavy, like pizza or a big sandwich, I get this really panicky feeling. I start worrying that I'll wake up bigger and slower. My work is physical, so I have to be up and down ladders and moving around rooms all day. I just get scared that if I put on weight, I won't be able to move around the way I need to for my job.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient confirms being afraid of gaining weight, describing panic and fear of waking up bigger after eating heavy meals.

turns.doctor_question: When you look at your body, do you feel like you are overweight?
turns.patient_response: Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel overweight. When I look in the mirror, I just... I see my normal body. I don't think I'm too big right now, I just want to make sure it stays that way. I guess I just check to make sure I haven't gained anything so I can keep working the way I do.

symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient explicitly denies having a distorted body image, stating they do not feel overweight or too big when looking in the mirror and simply see their normal body.

turns.doctor_question: Has your weight dropped to a level that a doctor has told you is below what’s healthy for you?

symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient minimizes the doctor's warning and others' concerns, stating they do not see it that way and rationalizing the low weight as just having 'leaned out'.
